name: host-tenant-binding
cost_provenance: measured 2026-09-30 on the dev workstation (win32, under concurrent cargo load), static mode; see docs/planning/project-checks-review-2026-09.md
question: Is every router merged in build_app classified and wired as its class requires? Public: bind_public_routes(apply_public_rate_limit(..)) with `.layer(cors` exactly where required (submission, attachments, board) and nowhere else; admin: bind_admin_routes; unbound: health + capabilities only. Unclassified or twice-merged routers fail. Probe B: admin_host_binding maps Tenant to 404, AdminAlias to a redirect, never 403, and gates X-Forwarded-Host. Probe C: one host->tenant resolution path. Absorbs public-route-ceiling and cors-allowlist-enforcement Probe A (2026-09-30).

output.schema: PASS or FAIL <n> with probe-level offender detail (file:line). Exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 environment error. A missing target is a FAIL, never a vacuous PASS.

consultation.typical_sessions_using: every commit that adds or rewires a public route, touches build_app, or changes the host layer

consumer_scope: feedbackmonk: anyone adding a public or admin route, and every reviewer of the hosting shape (FR-FBR-32/33). Green is the FR-FBR-32 exit gate.
fallback: Read .claude/project-oracles/host-tenant-binding/README.md: it lists each probe as rewritten on 2026-09-30 and what to check by hand; the `question` above is the one-paragraph form.

provenance.authored_by: DEFER-005 build lane (FR-FBR-32/33). Assertion block frozen at Task Zero, BEFORE any implementation existed, per the injecting brief's explicit instruction.
provenance.hardening_note: Adversarially self-tested during authoring: (1) dropping bind_public_routes from widget_config_router and bind_admin_routes from moderation_router -> Probe A FAIL naming both, exit 1; (2) flipping the cross-tenant refusal from 404 to 403 -> Probe B FAIL. Both restored and re-verified PASS. Probe A is parenthesis-balanced over `.merge(` arguments rather than regex-split, because the real arguments nest (bind_public_routes(apply_public_rate_limit(board_router(state), prl), hs)) and a naive split truncates at the first `)` -- which would have produced a silent false PASS. INTENTIONALLY_UNBOUND records the two deliberate exemptions (health_router, capabilities_router) with reasons, so a reviewer sees the exemptions rather than inferring them from absence.
provenance.rationale: DEC-FBR-13 chose tenant subdomains over path-based multi-tenancy for ONE decisive reason: origin isolation for the user-generated-content surface. That reason is bought only by BINDING -- resolution alone buys nothing, and its absence is invisible at runtime because a missing guard renders a perfectly correct-looking page of another tenant's feedback on your origin. No happy-path test can see it. multi-tenant-isolation-check does not cover it either: that oracle polices the REPOSITORY scope axis, and a router merged without the host guard passes it unchanged. This is detection-from-code over a second, orthogonal isolation axis introduced by FR-FBR-32.
